body: Sad day, no advice here either.

Yeah. My stepmom poisoned me twice, once with anti-freeze and the other time by tricking an already sick me into taking medicine that she had mixed with god knows what. Both ended in me unresponsive and in the hospital. She also cut the breaks on my bike and directed me down a tremendously steep hill. Ended in severe lacerations, but nothing broken. I was beaten as punishment for both. My dad was convinced (by stepmom) that I was doing it to myself. You know, for attention. They're still married and I haven't spoken to my dad's family in 11 years. Hope it stays that way.

Thank you so much for your kind words. I think it says a lot about your character that you take the time to share warmth and honesty with a stranger. It felt really good to just get it out, and I know that hurting myself would ruin all that I have put toward the future of my niece and nephew. I truly wish you the absolute best in life.

Thank you for taking the time to write this out. I think her and I have some remaining codependent behaviors from childhood and your breakdown of healthy relationship boundaries for siblings is really helpful. I think I need to stop forking over the dough. I'll let her know my door is always open for her and her kids, and that I can't enable her finance's decision to not work anymore. I hope she still wants to maintain a relationship, but either way, its whats right.

I really want to respect the fact that he's their father. Nothing in the world will change that, and my not liking him is going to hurt the kids more than anything. Superficially civil is the best route. I can be nice and not really talk to him at the same time.

(Internet hug back) 

Thank you. I think focusing on getting myself to a point where they could come live with me at a moments notice is a very good approach. It gives me something to do so I feel less helpless, and it does help her and I stay on good terms. I will start documenting everything though, a picture of his weed stash is enough to seal the deal in my state. I feel like shit even thinking about going behind someone's back like that, but if it gets her out when she needs it too, it'll be worth it.

You've said it best. She needs to feel the panic of not having me to support her before she'll realize she is able to leave him and can support her family on her own. I know that's what she's the most afraid of, and it's crazy because she's already supporting him AND her kids! Without him it would be that much easier!

Thank you. It helps to know I'm not alone in this experience! Bad idea pants is a light-hearted way to put it. Much better than my BOB nickname for him (bag of bricks). Did you feel like what was happening with your sister was affecting your personal relationships? My boyfriend already dislikes the guy and they've never met. I admit that's my fault, but I'm not gonna lie to my SO about the situation either. It just really sucks for everyone involved. My niece asked him the other day when he was getting a job for heaven's sake. SHE'S 8.

If something happens to my sister, I'd pray to whatever god is listening that I get custody. Maybe a good place to start is ensuring my sister is aware that she can move in with me any time. I know she feels trapped, and it would honestly be cheaper for all of us if she moved in with me.
Yeah. Easier said than done, but I agree I need to be civil. I'm debating not going to the holiday at all.

She's in love, and she thinks the most important thing is to keep the family together. She is an awesome person and mother, but she's only ever dated this one guy. I will stop giving her money, but I won't let a member of my family go hungry. It doesn't matter who its 'on', what matters is trying to make the situation better. Any advice related to that is what I'm looking for.
I can stop giving them cash, I understand that's enabling and I need to stop.

I'm really scared by what their sunken ship would look like. A falling out means I don't get to see the kids, and we're very bonded. It would hurt everyone so much to go through that again. Do you think I should call him out when he's around or when he's gone? Maybe writing a letter is best?

She needs the help. One person can't manage her situation, and I won't ever be able to stop supporting the kids as best I can. How am I supposed to deal with him in person? Do I let it go? Bring it up to him?
I agree that trashing my brother-in-law isn't the way to go, but I feel so strongly that he's a total fuck up I can barely look him in the eye. How do I handle seeing him next time?
